object.title: $q$-analogue of the Erdős Matching Conjecture
object.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ be the $n$-dimensional vector space over the finite field with $q$ elements, and let $\nu_q(\mathcal{V})$ denote the largest size of a matching of pairwise disjoint members of a family $\mathcal{V}$ of subspaces. **$q$-analogue Erdős Matching Conjecture.** If $\mathcal{V}$ is a family of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, $n\geq(s+1)k$, and $\nu_q(\mathcal{V})\leq s$, then

$$
|\mathcal{V}|\leq\min\left\{\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{k}-\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-1}{k},\;s\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-1}{k-1}\right\}.
$$

The paper explicitly presents this as an open problem and as a $q$-analogue of the Erdős Matching Conjecture.

object.title: Suffix-language characterization conjecture for FKM universal cycles
object.statement: Let $\textbf{T}(n,k)$ denote the set of strings of length $n$ over the paper's alphabet, and let $\textbf{S}\subseteq\textbf{T}(n,k)$ be closed under rotations. Given a string $\alpha\in\textbf{T}(n,k)$, an **$\alpha$-suffix language** is a set of strings such that, whenever $\beta=b_1\cdots b_n$ belongs to it and $\alpha=a_1\cdots a_n$, one has $b_m\leq a_m$ and $b_1\cdots b_{m-1}a_m\cdots a_n$ belongs to the set for every $1\leq m\leq n$. **Suffix-language characterization conjecture.** The FKM algorithm generates a universal cycle for $\textbf{S}$ if and only if the set of necklaces in $\textbf{S}$ is an $\alpha$-suffix language, where $\alpha$ is the lexicographically maximal necklace in $\textbf{S}$. This proposes a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of the rotation-closed languages for which the FKM algorithm produces a universal cycle.

object.title: Ihringer's conjecture on largest $s$-EM-families of $k$-spaces
object.literal_statement: Let an $s$-EM-family of $k$-spaces be a family of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ with matching number at most $s$, and let an intersecting family be one whose members are pairwise non-disjoint. **Ihringer's conjecture.** For $n\geq2k$, if $Y$ is a largest $s$-EM-family of $k$-spaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, then $Y$ is the union of $s$ intersecting families or its complement. The source notes that Ihringer proved this under an additional quantitative condition, but the general conjecture remains unresolved there.

statement_provenance.raw_token: "Let $H$ be a finite group. A **gain-graphic matroid** is a frame matroid obtained from a graph with edge gains in $H$, and a class is **well-quasi-ordered** when it has neither an infinite strict descending sequence nor an infinite antichain under the relevant minor relation. **Finite-group gain-graphic well-quasi-order conjecture.** The class of $H$-gain graphic matroids is well-quasi-ordered. If true, every minor-closed class of $H$-gain-graphic matroids would have at most finitely many excluded minors that are themselves $H$-gain-graphic. The source says this is widely believed and expected to be approachable, at least for abelian $H$, while the corresponding assertion fails for infinite groups."
